mechanism_claims.claim_text: CP1 and CP1(1-29) retain similar bactericidal activity in Table 1, so the C-terminal Pro30/Arg31 deletion has limited effect on the measured MBC phenotype under the paper's assay conditions.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=7:Comparison of the Activity of CP1 (WT) and CP1 (1-29);xml:table=1

mechanism_claims.limitations: MBC values support phenotype comparison, not a standalone molecular target mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: NMR in DPC micelles supports a long alpha-helical membrane-mimetic structure for CP1 and CP1(1-29), with DPC interaction over much of the peptide length.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: CP1 (WT) and CP1 (1-29) in DPC micelles

mechanism_claims.limitations: DPC micelles are a membrane-mimetic environment and do not by themselves prove bacterial membrane disruption in cells.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper directly tests DNA binding by electrophoretic mobility shift assay; CP1 WT binds DNA more strongly than CP1(1-29), supporting DNA binding as a plausible contributor to antimicrobial activity.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=7:Comparison of the Activity of CP1 (WT) and CP1 (1-29);xml:fig=6;xml:sec=13:DNA-Binding Experiments

mechanism_claims.limitations: The authors state that many details of CP1-DNA binding remain unresolved; final curation should not overclaim DNA binding as the sole killing mechanism.

caution_findings.note: NMR/DPC and DNA mobility-shift evidence support mechanism context, but the paper does not resolve a single antimicrobial killing pathway.
